hints: Write each altitude using side AB and a sine: AD comes from the angle at B, and BE from the angle at A.
AD = AB sin θ and BE = AB sin 45°.
1.why:
In right triangle ABD, AD = AB sin B = AB sin θ. In right triangle ABE, BE = AB sin A = AB sin 45° = AB/√2.

AD/BE = sin θ ÷ (1/√2) = √2 sin θ.

hints: Let their times be 5k, 8k and 10k hours. Together they finish in 4 × 8 = 32 hours. Use that to find k.
Anu and Tanu then work 6 × 6⅔ = 40 hours together. Find what's left and give it to Manu.
2.why:
Combined hourly rate = (1/5 + 1/8 + 1/10)/k = 17/(40k). 32 × 17/(40k) = 1, so k = 13.6.

Anu + Tanu rate = 13/(40k). In 40 hours they do 13/k = 13/13.6 of the job, leaving 0.6/13.6 = 3/68.

Manu takes 10k = 136 hours for the whole job, so 136 × 3/68 = 6 hours.

hints: A regular n-gon has interior angle 180 − 360/n degrees.
Let A have n sides and B have 2n. Set the angles' ratio to 3 : 4.
Write a = 6 − 2b, then a + b in terms of b alone.
Both a and b must be ≥ 0. What range does that allow for b?
4.why:
a + b = 6 − b, with 0 ≤ b ≤ 3.

So a + b runs from 3 (b = 3) to 6 (b = 0).

Average of max and min = (3 + 6)/2 = 4.5.

hints: His yearly target is 12 × 550 = 6600.
Work out what he saves in the first nine months, then what each of the last three months must save.
5.why:
First nine months: 9 × (4000 − 3500) = 4500 saved.

He needs 2100 more over 3 months, so 700 a month. With expenses of 3700, he must earn 3700 + 700 = 4400.

hints: Use numbers: start with 1 litre of syrup in the first container and 1 litre of milk in the second.
Track syrup and milk separately through each of the three transfers.
6.why:
Transfer 1: 0.5 syrup goes to the second. Second = 0.5 syrup + 1 milk.

Transfer 2: half of that comes back: 0.25 syrup + 0.5 milk. First = 0.75 syrup + 0.5 milk; second = 0.25 syrup + 0.5 milk.

Transfer 3: half the first goes over: 0.375 syrup + 0.25 milk. Second = 0.625 syrup + 0.75 milk, which is 5 : 6.

hints: On day n the count is multiplied by (1 + 1/n) = (n + 1)/n.
Multiply these factors from day 2 to day m. Most of them cancel.
Replacing a<sub>1</sub> with 6a<sub>1</sub> adds 5a<sub>1</sub> to the total, which raises the average by 100. So 5a<sub>1</sub> = 100N.
a<sub>1</sub> is the smallest number, so it can't be more than the average 300. What does that say about N?
8.why:
a1 = 20N, and a1 ≤ 300 gives N ≤ 15.

N = 1 fails: then a1 would have to be 300 and 20 at once. Every N from 2 to 15 works (for N = 15, all numbers are 300).

So there are 14 possible values of a1.

hints: Let the third root be s. Use the sum of products of roots taken two at a time: −r<sup>2</sup> + rs − rs.
That gives r<sup>2</sup>. Then the product of the roots gives s, and the sum of the roots gives c.
9.why:
Pairwise products: −r2 = −10/5, so r2 = 2.

Product: r × (−r) × s = −9/5, so 2s = 9/5 and s = 9/10.

Sum: r − r + s = −c/5, so c = −5 × 9/10 = −9/2.

hints: f(x) + f(x − 1) = 1 means f(x) = f(x − 2): f has one value on even numbers and another on odd numbers.
x<sup>2</sup> − x = x(x − 1) is always even. So f(even) = 5. What is f(odd)?
The other three split 70% of the votes cast in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Work out each share.
Compare the winner with the second-highest. The gap of 2512 is a percentage of votes cast, and votes cast are 80% of registered voters.
11.why:
The three shares are 70/6, 140/6 and 35 percent. So the winner has 35% and second place has 30%.

5% of votes cast = 2512, so votes cast = 50240.

Registered voters = 50240 / 0.8 = 62800. 50240 is the trap: that's votes cast.

hints: Count 4-digit, 5-digit and 6-digit numbers separately.
4-digit numbers above 2000 must start with 2, 3, 4 or 5. Longer numbers just can't start with 0.
12.why:
4-digit: 4 × 5 × 4 × 3 = 240. 5-digit: 5 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 600. 6-digit: 5 × 5! = 600.

Total = 1440. (2000 itself repeats 0, so there's nothing to remove.)

hints: a! divides b! exactly when a ≤ b.
So you need n! ≤ 15000. Work out factorials.
Let t = log<sub>2</sub> n. Then log<sub>4</sub> n = t/2.
The fraction is 2(4 − t)/(6 − t). A fraction is negative when the top and bottom have opposite signs.
14.why:
(4 − t) and (6 − t) have opposite signs only when 4 < t < 6.

So 16 < n < 64, which gives n = 17 to 63.

That's 47 integers.

hints: Let c be correct, w wrong, u unattempted. c + w + u = 75 and 3c − w + u = 97.
Subtracting gives c − w = 11. Unattempted beats attempted means u ≥ 38, so c + w ≤ 37.
15.why:
c = ((c + w) + 11)/2. To make c as big as possible, make c + w as big as allowed: 37.

Then c = 24, w = 13 and u = 38. Check: 72 − 13 + 38 = 97.

The maximum is 24.

hints: The five marks add to 190. Three are above 32; the fourth is at most 32, and Amit is below the fourth.
For Amit's highest: give the fourth student 32 and Amit 31, then check the top three can make up the rest. For his lowest: make the top three as big as possible.
16.why:
Highest: Amit 31, fourth 32. The top three need 127, for example 41, 42, 44. That works, so the maximum is 31.

Lowest: top three = 50 + 49 + 48 = 147, leaving 43. With the fourth at 32, Amit gets 11.

Difference = 31 − 11 = 20.

hints: a<sup>b</sup> = 1 in three ways: a = 1; b = 0 with a ≠ 0; or a = −1 with b even.
Check each case with whole-number x.
17.why:
Base 1: x2 = 11, no integer.

Exponent 0: x2 − 3x − 10 = 0 gives x = 5 or −2, and the base isn't 0. Two solutions.

Base −1: x = ±3. The exponent is −10 for x = 3 and 8 for x = −3, both even. Two more. Total = 4.

hints: Take a capital of 15, so the fractions are whole: 3, 5 and the rest, 7.
Add up one year's interest, then see how many years it takes to reach 15.
18.why:
Yearly interest: 3 × 6% + 5 × 10% + 7 × 1% = 0.18 + 0.5 + 0.07 = 0.75.

That's 5% of 15 a year, so it takes 15 / 0.75 = 20 years.

hints: The AP has first term 3 and difference 4, so A<sub>n</sub> = n(2n + 1) = 2n<sup>2</sup> + n.
Sum 2n<sup>2</sup> + n for n = 1 to 25 using Σn<sup>2</sup> = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6.
A quadratic that's never negative and is 0 at x = 2 must touch the x-axis there.
So f(x) = a(x − 2)<sup>2</sup>. Use f(4) = 6 to find a.
ADC and ABD have the same height from A, so their areas are in the ratio DC : BD. That gives BD = 2 and DC = 1.
Use the cosine rule in triangle ADC with angle C = 60°.
South and west are at right angles, so the distance apart is the hypotenuse.
With speeds v and v + 6, after 2 hours: (2v)<sup>2</sup> + (2v + 12)<sup>2</sup> = 60<sup>2</sup>.
22.why:
v2 + (v + 6)2 = 900 gives v2 + 6v − 432 = 0, so (v + 24)(v − 18) = 0.

The slower ship goes 18 km/h. Check: 36 and 48 km after 2 hours, and √(362 + 482) = 60.
